evidence.why: Exact fit test, copy and update.

facts.rationale: Preserves normal saturation behavior while removing an unconditional safety claim.
facts.value: Selects the full request when CharsWritten + char_num <= MaxCharCount, otherwise MaxCharCount - CharsWritten; copies that amount and advances CharsWritten by it. With a valid controller and nonoverflowing addition, this saturates at capacity and subsequent requests copy zero bytes. The implementation does not guard addition overflow or an initially out-of-range count.

evidence.why: Dispatch, typed stores and output transitions.

facts.rationale: Corrects modifier overgeneralization while preserving output ordering and exceptional branches.
facts.value: Processes literals and conversions until completion, returning -1 immediately on any sink failure. %n consumes a pointer and stores the logical count only for normal, short, long and long-long options; accepted hh has no store case. The c branch emits one byte from an int even for accepted lc. Right justification emits leading spaces or zeroes, moving an initial plus/minus before zero fill; left justification emits trailing spaces. Invalid specifications and failed conversions write the remaining format beginning at the current '%' literally and return immediately.

facts.rationale: Documents the actual boundary branches without claiming universal ties-to-even correctness.
facts.value: A negative requested length immediately produces positive zero with exponent 0 and one digit '0'; a length covering the significand leaves it unchanged. Otherwise the first discarded digit and remaining suffix determine carry. Exact halves use p[-1] parity, implementing retained-digit ties-to-even when new_length is positive; at zero retained length p[-1] is before sig.text, not a retained digit. Carry propagates through retained digits while trailing zeroes are trimmed. Escaping carry increments the exponent and sets the significand to '1'; no remaining nonzero digit produces canonical positive zero.

evidence.why: Controller copy behavior and wrapper initialization/termination.

facts.rationale: Corrects initialization wording and preserves exact termination arithmetic and exceptional cases.
facts.value: Assigns osc.CharStr = s, osc.MaxCharCount = n and osc.CharsWritten = 0, then passes the local controller, __StringWrite, format and arg to __pformatter. The callback tracks copied bytes separately from the formatter's logical count and can copy up to n bytes, not n-1. Afterwards the wrapper unconditionally executes s[(end < n) ? end : n - 1] = '\0' and returns end unchanged. There is no zero-capacity or negative-result guard; the index expression mixes int and size_t and must not be interpreted as universally safe bounded termination.
